citations.narrative:
The facility is not maintaining the shift doors for both species of macaques; the doors aren’t free of excessive rust. The
outer areas of the metal shift doors are reddish brown and have a pockmarked appearance. The metal bars attached to
the cement wall that allow the door to shift open and closed are also a deep reddish brown with pocket marked areas. The
non-human primates can come into contact with the rusted surfaces. Rusted primary enclosure surfaces can lose
structural integrity over time and cannot be properly cleaned and sanitized. The licensee must ensure that any surfaces
that come into contact with non-human primates are free of excessive rust that prevents the required cleaning and
sanitization, or that affects the structural strength of the surfaces.
Correct by September 18, 2026

The outdoor housing facilities for the goats are not being maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury. The
wood boards making up the barn doors to the goat's indoor area are deteriorating at the bottom. The wood is missing
paint and has several splintered pieces creating sharp points. The damage is such that there is an obvious difference in
thickness between the intact wood and the damaged wood. Failure to maintain housing facilities so that they are
structurally sound and in good repair can increase the possibility of injury to the animals.
Correct by maintaining the housing facilities in good repair to protect the goats from injury.

The facility failed to regulate the ambient temperatures and protect the animals from temperature extremes in the indoor
portion of the enclosures for the two Spectacled Bears and the two Jaguars.
At the time of the inspection, at approximately 1 PM, USDA inspector felt a noticeable increase in temperature as they
entered the building for the indoor enclosures of the two Jaguars and the two Spectacled Bears. Using the government
issued Kestrel, USDA inspector measured a range of temperature inside the building from 124.9 to 127 degrees
Fahrenheit. The facility representative was unsure if the air conditioning was broken by the bears or if the building didn’t
have AC.
The Spectacled Bears are housed exclusively outdoors for exhibition hours during the day, and the jaguars have access
to both the outdoor and indoor portions of their enclosure during the day. Both the bears and the jaguars are confined only
to the indoor portion of this enclosure after exhibition hours and at night. The facility reports that they have been doing
nothing differently overnight to mitigate the high temperatures.
At 10am on August 17, 2026, the National Weather Service recorded a temperature for the area of 88 degrees F with a
heat index at 102 degrees F. At 4 pm the temperature had risen to 96.1 degrees F with a heat index of 108 degrees F.
From 7 pm to 10 am (the evening of August 17, 2026, to the morning of August 18, 2026), the National Weather Service
recorded temperatures ranging from 90 to 87.1 degrees F with a heat index of 97 degrees F to 99 degrees F respectively.
Neither species had the option to escape the heat while in the indoor portion of the enclosure, however, they didn’t exhibit
signs of heat distress. After speaking with the USDA inspector, the facility intends to leave doors open to increase airflow
at night. Prolonged exposure to extreme temperatures can be detrimental to the health of the animals and cause
discomfort.
The facility must ensure that indoor housing facilities be sufficiently regulated by heating or cooling to protect the animals
from extremes of temperature and to provide for their health and prevent their discomfort.
Correct by August 24, 2026

The facility is not keeping the premises clean and in good repair in order to protect the animals from injury and to facilitate
the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.
The building housing the ambassador animals such as prairie dogs, chinchillas, and a ferret was in disarray with animal
enclosures placed behind and amongst storage and building materials, enrichment materials, office supplies, and other
paraphernalia. In an HVAC closet across from the chinchilla enclosure, the USDA inspector identified an accumulation of
rodent feces, discarded lettuce and hay. The accumulation of additional materials can provide areas that harbor disease-
transmitting pests that could be health risks to the animals. Additionally, the building housing a male Zebra had an
excessive accumulation of cobwebs in the rafters, on the ceilings and around the box fans. The box fan had a thick layer
of brown dust over the front panel. Accumulations of dust and cobwebs indicate inadequate cleaning and the presence of
pests that may pose health risks to the animals.
Correct by ensuring that premises (buildings and grounds) are kept clean, in good repair and accumulations of trash are
placed in designated areas and cleared as necessary in order to protect the animals from injury, protect their health, and
to facilitate prescribed husbandry practices.
Correct by September 18, 2026

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an environmental enhancement plan (EEP) approved by the current attending veterinarian. The
current attending veterinarian started on June 8, 2026, and has not approved the environmental enhancement plan.
Failure to implement and follow an EEP as outlined can negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals.
Exhibitors must develop, document, and follow a species-appropriate plan for environmental enhancement that is
approved by the attending veterinarian to adequately promote the psychological well-being of birds.
Correct by August 31, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
